critical_issues: No fixed term creates ongoing obligation until terminated
Work for hire means no portfolio rights without permission
Only 2 free revision rounds (reasonable but could be limiting)
Additional revisions at $75/hour could add up
strengths: Reasonable liability cap at 3 months fees
Either party can terminate with 14 days notice
Pro-rated payment for work in progress
Clear rate structure and deliverable expectations
Company responsible for factual accuracy of their info
ip_concerns: Work for hire - Company owns all content
Portfolio use requires permission (restrictive but negotiable)
Cannot reuse content for other clients
Standard for content writing but limits portfolio building
Originality warranty requires Contractor ensure no plagiarism
termination_terms: Complete work in progress or get paid pro-rata
Payment for all completed approved work
workflow_concerns: Company must provide feedback within 5 days or content deemed approved
2 revision rounds may not be enough for complex topics
Additional revisions at $75/hour is fair but could inflate costs

confidentiality.scope: Business plans, unpublished content, strategic info

rationale: This is a fair, balanced content writing contract. The liability is reasonably capped, indemnification is mutual, termination terms are balanced, and the non-compete is limited to 6 months and direct competitors only. The compensation is market-rate for quality content writing. The 2-year confidentiality and work-for-hire IP terms are industry standard. Main concerns are portfolio rights requiring permission and the ongoing nature with no fixed term.
suggested_improvements: Add explicit portfolio rights (can use with anonymized client name)
Consider 3 revision rounds instead of 2 for complex content
Add payment terms for late payment (interest)
Specify response time expectations for urgent requests
Add provision for content usage rights attribution if desired
acceptable_as_is: Yes, this contract is acceptable with only minor improvements needed
